- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in next 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline after peak), model overreacts; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% for next 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 2–5% downward bias for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast with sentiment trend direction for next 3–5 days.
